title: fanoutqa: Which of the world's five highest mountains were first successfully climbed by British mountaineers? (14b7db2b18bf897c)

chat_history.content: Which of the world's five highest mountains were first successfully climbed by British mountaineers?

content.content:
The user asks: "Which of the world's five highest mountains were first successfully climbed by British mountaineers?" So we need to identify the world's five highest mountains (the eight-thousanders? Actually the five highest mountains overall: Everest (8848m), K2 (8611m), Kangchenjunga (8586m), Lhotse (8516m), Makalu (8485m). Then determine which of those were first successfully climbed by British mountaineers.

We need to know the first ascents: Everest first ascent 1953 by Sir Edmund Hillary (New Zealander) and Tenzing Norgay (Sherpa) – not British (though Hillary was from New Zealand, which was part of Commonwealth but not British). K2 first ascent 1954 by Italian Lino Lacedelli and Achille Compagnoni – not British. Kangchenjunga first ascent 1955 by Joe Brown and George Band – both British. Lhotse first ascent 1956 by a Swiss/Austrian team (Ernst Reiss and Fritz Luchsinger) – not British. Makalu first ascent 1955 by French expedition (Jean Franco, Lionel Terray) – not British.

Thus only Kangchenjunga among the top five was first climbed by British mountaineers. However, need to check if any other top five had British involvement? The first ascent of Everest was by a British expedition (the 1953 British Everest Expedition) but the climbers were from New Zealand and Nepal, but the expedition was British-led. The question: "first successfully climbed by British mountaineers" – ambiguous: meaning the climbers were British. So Kangchenjunga is the answer. Might also mention that the first ascent of Everest was led by British but the climbers were not British. So answer: Kangchenjunga only.

Thus respond accordingly.

content:
**Kangchenjunga** – the world’s third‑highest peak (8 586 m) – is the only one of the five highest mountains that was first summited by British mountaineers.

| Rank | Mountain | Height (m) | First successful ascent | Nationality of the summit climbers |
|------|----------|-----------|--------------------------|------------------------------------|
| 1    | **Mount Everest** | 8 848 | 29 May 1953 (Edmund Hillary – New Zealand; Tenzing Norgay – Sherpa) | Not British (though the expedition was British‑led) |
| 2    | **K2** | 8 611 | 31 July 1954 (Lino Lacedelli & Achille Compagnoni – Italy) | Not British |
| 3    | **Kangchenjunga** | 8 586 | 25 May 1955 (Joe Brown & George Band – United Kingdom) | **British** |
| 4    | **Lhotse** | 8 516 | 18 May 1956 (Ernst Reiss & Fritz Luchsinger – Switzerland/Austria) | Not British |
| 5    | **Makalu** | 8 485 | 15 May 1955 (Jean Franco & Lionel Terray – France) | Not British |

So, among the world’s five highest peaks, **Kangchenjunga** is the sole mountain whose first ascent was achieved by British climbers.
